new_findings.input: d64recheck/U23/n4/server.py: module level has `from pathlib import Path`. Inside `def register(m):` there is a local `from pathlib import Path` (same target) plus `from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context`, then `@m.tool(annotations={"readOnlyHint": True}) def put_localimp(path: Path): path.write_text("x")`.
new_findings.observed: On e9afc10, put_localimp has 2 pathlib.Path.write_text FS_WRITE rows, D1 矛 fs_write. On f720a4b it has no FS_WRITE row, so D1 is 内. _shadowed_annotation sees `Path` bound in the enclosing register() by the local import and drops the seed, even though that import resolves to the same pathlib.Path. The pre-U23 base 9030919 also had no row.
new_findings.expected: D1 矛 fs_write, as on e9afc10. At runtime the annotation is evaluated in register's scope as pathlib.Path, FastMCP builds a Path, and write_text writes the file under readOnlyHint.
new_findings.plausibility: Low to medium. Local imports inside register(mcp)-style functions are a known pattern (CLAUDE.md lists nested definitions and conditional imports as pitfalls). The implementer disclosed the check as conservative, but it also drops seeds when the enclosing binding resolves to the same external target, and the whole U23 gain (pathlib rows, lifespan Context seed) is lost there. `_bound_names` also walks nested bodies, including other methods' locals in a class scope, which Python does not use for annotation evaluation.
new_findings.proposed_fix: In _shadowed_annotation, when the only binding of a name across the enclosing scopes is a single level-0 Import/ImportFrom directly in that scope's body, resolve it to its ext dotted name and let _typed_seed / the Context check use that. Or treat the name as not shadowed when the dotted name equals the module-level resolution. Keep treating every other binding (def/class/assignment/param/global, or two or more bindings) as shadowed. When walking a ClassDef, count only direct class-body bindings, not bindings inside methods.

new_findings.input: d64recheck/U23/n5/server.py: `ROOT = "/srv"`; `class ReqF(BaseModel): path: str = Field(description=f"file under {ROOT}")`; `class ReqE(BaseModel): path: str; mode: Mode = Mode.A` (Mode is an in-tree str Enum). Tools with destructiveHint=False call `open(req.path, "w")`.
new_findings.observed: On e9afc10, wf and we are D2 矛 fs_writeout_model_path. On f720a4b both are D2 不 fs_writeout_model_path_opaque. _static_class_value rejects the f-string description and the Enum-attribute default, so the whole class counts as hooked and req.path becomes MODEL/opaque. The control ReqD, whose Field uses only literal kwargs, stays 矛.
new_findings.expected: 矛. description/title/examples/json_schema_extra do not change validated values. A BaseModel field default that is an Enum member (no __set__, not a validator) does not replace a value the model supplies.
new_findings.plausibility: Medium for f-string or constant-expression descriptions and Enum defaults in MCP pydantic models. The error is on the fail-closed side (矛 becomes 不, the same as base 9030919). The implementer disclosed the Enum and nested-Call cases; the doc-only Field kwargs are an extra case of the same over-rejection.
new_findings.proposed_fix: In the Field/PrivateAttr/field branch, require a static value only for `default` (and default_factory), and skip the check for documentation-only kwargs (description, title, examples, json_schema_extra, alias, serialization_alias). If needed, accept an Enum member of an in-tree Enum class that has no __set__/__get__ as a static default for the pydantic family only. Keep the current strict rule for dataclass defaults (descriptor risk).

summary:
All six findings (A1, A2, P1, P2, P3, S1) are closed. I ran each reviewer tree against the fixed commit f720a4b and against e9afc10 (git archive into scratch), using runner.run and then manifest_json, and checked the 矛/不/内 status of each unit. I also ran extra trees n1 through n8, with the pre-U23 base 9030919 added as a third column.

On the part the fix touched, I found no new 矛 anywhere and no increase in resolution: every change moved values to opaque or MODEL/opaque, which dparse can only turn into influenced, so 不. I checked the parts of dparse and effects that could give 矛: _choice, _host_class, _http_method, the D1/D2/D3 NET/SPAWN/EXEC checks and the shell/mode reads. All of them require resolved values. Receiver rows are kept, including DB, pathlib and NET rows through in-tree classes, dataclass nesting and the low-level server.

The fix did introduce two problems, both on the fail-closed side:
- R1: the S1 scope check drops the seed when the enclosing register() function locally imports the same Path. The D1 矛 fs_write row disappears and the result is 内, which is also what base gave.
- R2: the static-value rule rejects f-string descriptions and Enum defaults, so the whole class loses its seed and 矛 becomes 不.

R3 is an existing hole, not caused by the fix: the prefix connection for module-level shared state is still 内.

Beyond the findings:
1. Test suite:
   - `tests/test_d64_u23_entry_seeding.py::test_fix_ls_rebound_unreadable_const` fails on f720a4b. The status is still 不, but the reason is now db_sql_model_opaque instead of the expected db_sql_unreadable, because A1 made the leaf MODEL. The test expectation was not updated.
   - `tests/test_f0a_defects.py::test_known_deep_module_dict_url_is_not_op_resolved` (@KNOWN, strict xfail) now passes because of A2, so the suite marks it as a failure. The mark should be removed.
   - `test_val_fixtures::test_precondition_known_unmet_keys_exist` already fails on d76f693, so it is unrelated.
2. Speed: `_bound_names` is not cached and walks the whole enclosing function for every parameter. A tree with 300 tools nested in register() (n8) went from 0.9s to 27.6s; the profile puts about 97% of the time in `_bound_names`. It is not a correctness problem and nothing drops in the scan scripts, since they have no per-tree timeout.
